translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 29.11.2017 (radio)
Britain's Prince William is visiting Finland. This year's Finlandia Prizes have been awarded. The Finnish school in Winterthur congratulates Finland.
## Prince William
![Niinistö and Prince William](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9954217)
Open image viewer
Prince William brought the President a letter from the Queen of Britain. Photo: Jussi Nukari / Lehtikuva
Britain's Prince William is visiting Finland. William came to Finland on Wednesday.
At the start of the visit, the prince went to the Presidential Palace. There William met President Sauli Niinistö.
Prince William brought President Niinistö a letter from Queen Elizabeth. William said that the letter is the Queen's message to a good friend. Queen Elizabeth is Prince William's grandmother.
On Wednesday evening, Prince William is having dinner with Finland's presidential couple at Mäntyniemi. Mäntyniemi is the Finnish President's residence in Helsinki.
Prince William's visit continues on Thursday. For example, he will visit a Finnish school in Lauttasaari in Helsinki.
On Thursday afternoon, William will visit the Christmas markets at Senate Square and in the Esplanadi park in Helsinki. Then Finns will have a chance to see a real prince.
## The Finlandia Prizes
This year's Finlandia Prizes have been awarded. The Finlandia Prizes are given to people who have written the best Finnish books of the year.
![The winner of the Finlandia Prize for fiction, Juha Hurme, in Helsinki on Wednesday 29 November.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9954500)
Open image viewer
Juha Hurme received the Finlandia Prize for fiction. Photo: Roni Rekomaa / Lehtikuva

This year the Finlandia Prize for fiction went to Juha Hurme. He received the prize for a book called Niemi (The Cape). The book is a funny story about the world and Finland over 14 billion years. The book begins when the world is born and ends in the year 1809.

![Journalist Riitta Kylänpää won the Finlandia Prize for non-fiction with her work Pentti Linkola – The Man and the Legend in Helsinki on 29 November](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9954262)
Open image viewer
Riitta Kylänpää received the Finlandia Prize for non-fiction. Photo: Roni Rekomaa / Lehtikuva
Journalist Riitta Kylänpää received the Finlandia Prize for non-fiction. Kylänpää has written a non-fiction book about the life of the Finnish environmental philosopher Pentti Linkola.

![ The Finlandia Prize for children's and young people's literature was won by illustrator and graphic designer Sanna Mander with her book Avain hukassa (The Lost Key).](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9954341)
Open image viewer
Sanna Mander received the Finlandia Prize for children's literature. Photo: Roni Rekomaa / Lehtikuva

The Finlandia Prize for children's literature went to Sanna Mander. Mander's children's book "Avain hukassa" (The Lost Key) tells about the different residents of a block of flats. Mander has also made the book's beautiful pictures.
All the Finlandia Prizes are 30,000 euros.
## The Finnish school in Winterthur
![Two boys](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9953587)
Open image viewer
Pupils of the Finnish school in Winterthur. Photo: Yle
The Finnish schools' congratulations to 100-year-old Finland continue.

A large number of Finnish children and young people live in different parts of the world and study the Finnish language and Finnish culture in Finnish schools. They are sending greetings to Finland, and the newest greetings come from the Finnish school in Winterthur, Switzerland.

You can watch the greetings from the Finnish school in Winterthur on the Clear News website at yle.fi/selkouutiset, in the Finland 100 section. The greetings can also be found on the Clear News Facebook page.
**Greetings from the Finnish school in Winterthur**
